stimulus.text: Epidemic disease killed enormous numbers of Native people who had no immunity to European illnesses. The encomienda depended on Native workers, and disease destroyed that workforce. With Native labor collapsing, and with Las Casas's reforms making it harder to exploit Native workers, Spain turned to a new source of coerced workers: enslaved Africans, brought in under the asiento, the Crown's monopoly contract for supplying enslaved people to Spanish America. The demand for coerced labor never went away; what changed was who was forced to work.

stem: The New Laws of 1542 limited the encomienda but did not end forced Native labor, and Spain soon expanded African slavery instead. What does this outcome best illustrate?

options.text: That Spanish reformers had no real influence on colonial policy at all.
That the New Laws actually strengthened and expanded the encomienda system.
That dependence on coerced labor outlasted any single reform of the system.
That Native peoples throughout the colonies were fully liberated by the New Laws.

instruction: Pick one option from the stimulus and stem only. Do not open the question file.
